title: Semantic and Expressive Variation in Image Captions Across Languages

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing the semantic content (via scene graphs extracting objects, relationships, and attributes) and expressive dimensions (via linguistic metrics like concreteness, authenticity, tone, and embedding space coverage) of human and model-generated image captions across seven different languages.

Evaluating differences in visual perception and description by analyzing how speakers of different languages emphasize different visual concepts (e.g., focal objects versus background relationships) in image captions, highlighting the limitations of an English-only 'perceptual monoculture'.
